corpusSummary: The corpus spans social-science applications of large language models across health, education, governance, and everyday life. It highlights methodological uses of LLMs for data processing and analysis, examines human–AI interaction and trust, explores AI-enabled health information and education, and foregrounds equity, ethics, and governance. It also notes limitations in reliability, embodiment, and cultural adequacy, underscoring calls for validation and transparent practices.

themes.name: AI as methodological catalyst in social science
themes.description: Papers show LLMs enabling data extraction, coding, cross-domain transfer, and simulations, with emphasis on validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Research across health, education, work, and daily life analyzes trust, perceived humanness, embodiment, peer effects, and networked adoption shaping user experience.

themes.name: AI in health, education, and public communication
themes.description: Studies address AI-generated health information, patient education, AI tutoring, and AI-assisted public communication, balancing opportunities with safety and quality concerns.

themes.name: Equity, ethics, governance, and fairness in large language models
themes.description: A consistent focus on equity-first governance, bias and fairness analyses, and methodological standards to govern responsible AI use.

emergingKeywords: AI in education and health communications
